claims.sourceText: Memorandum Opinion, Kean v. NASA, 27 March 2007, Background section
claims.text: Her FOIA request of 31 January 2003 sought documents on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the 'Fragology Files' for 1962 to 1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and 'Cosmos 96'.

claims.sourceText: Memorandum Opinion, Kean v. NASA, Dkt. 45, 27 March 2007, pp. 1-2 and Conclusion
claims.text: The court's 27 March 2007 memorandum opinion states that NASA admits its first two searches were inadequate, and holds that the agency 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate', denying summary judgment in part.

edges.label: Two FOIA-first approaches to the same concealment question
edges.note: Cameron requests presidential and agency paper and publishes null returns; Kean litigated a null return to a judicial finding of inadequate search. Reasoning: both treat the absence of records as the evidentiary object rather than as an obstacle.

edges.label: The litigation was about the Kecksburg records specifically
edges.note: The underlying FOIA request of 31 January 2003 sought records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96.

edges.label: Project Moon Dust records were an express object of the FOIA request
edges.note: Moon Dust - the programme for recovery of foreign space and aerospace debris - is named in the request as reproduced in the court's Background section.

edges.label: Plaintiff who forced a court-supervised NASA records search
edges.note: Kean filed the complaint on 9 December 2003, obtained a 27 March 2007 finding that NASA had not shown its searches adequate, settled in part on 16 October 2007 and litigated status reports until dismissal on 24 August 2009.

edges.label: Gordon's witness pool underwrote the evidentiary premise of the suit
edges.note: The claim that something was recovered at Kecksburg, and therefore that records should exist, rests on the local testimony Gordon assembled. Reasoning: no document independently establishes a recovery, so the suit's factual premise is his witness base.
